successors.name: Teutonic Order
successors.text: Semigallia: the lower Mūša and Lielupe valleys, south-central Latvia and northern Lithuania, with Mežotne, Tērvete and Dobele

ledger.x: 1236: the Battle of Saule ends the Brothers' campaign.

1236: the contest continues against the successor Order (the Livonian branch of the Teutonic Order); the page dates no campaign that holds ground, so the land stays Semigallian, contested at confidence 1.
1254: the contest gives way to partial Order control (see the next entry).
1254: the Livonian Order partly subdues the Semigallians.
1279: Duke Nameisis rises with Lithuanian support.

1279-1290: the revolt under Nameisis reopens the contest; 'In the 1280s, the Livonian Order started a massive campaign against the Semigallians'; in 1287 'around 1400 Semigallians attacked a crusader stronghold in Ikšķile and plundered nearby lands', the main battle being near the Garoza river.
1290: the contest ends with the loss of the land (next entry).
1290: the Semigallians burn their last castle at Sidrabė and leave.
1290: Semigallian independence ends with the burning of Sidrabė.

wars.name: Livonian Crusade
wars.outcome: The Semigallians attacked the crusaders retreating from Saule (1236), were partly subdued by the Livonian Order in 1254, revolted under Nameisis in 1279, attacked Ikšķile in 1287 and ended their resistance by burning their last castle at Sidrabė in 1290.

certainty.note: Tribal lands without a boundary on the page; Semigallia is drawn as the Zemgale planning region plus a circle in northern Lithuania.
